title: After release, the first weeks predict a top-10 hit; before release, trends add nothing
body:
AFTER RELEASE · FIRST WEEKS ON THE HOT 100 → TOP 10?

InputAUCF1
year, month, artist history only.59.15
first week (debut position).75.40
first 2 weeks.85.53
first 3 weeks.89.61
first 4 weeks.92.67

31,925 songs, 16 % reach the top 10. Random Forest on positions, best rank, slope and acceleration + context; 5×3 CV, every gain 15/15 folds, p < 10⁻⁶.

Not trivial: on songs not yet in the top 10 after 3 weeks, AUC .87; trained before 2000 and tested after, .85. keep

BEFORE RELEASE · MARKET TREND ON THE KAGGLE BENCHMARK

Distance of a song's audio to the previous decade's hits, and whether it moves in the direction of the trend.

+0.1pt

on top of the main model, p = .66. remove

Per-feature deviation: +0.5 (p = .006, indicative). On audio alone the trend adds +1.8 — less than the decade itself (+2.0): it only carries era, which the model already has.

Time series help once a song is out: its first weeks are the best predictor we found. Before release, they add nothing to artist history and era.
